patterns.name: Distributed Flow Under Variable Demand
patterns.abstractDescription: Resources flow through a network of constrained pathways toward distributed destinations. Demand fluctuates, capacity is limited, and congestion emerges when flow exceeds local capacity.

examples.problem: City traffic congestion during peak hours
examples.solution: Adaptive traffic signals, congestion pricing, alternate route distribution
examples.outcome: 30% reduction in peak congestion in Singapore

examples.solution: Vasodilation, collateral vessel formation, heart rate adaptation
examples.outcome: Continuous oxygen delivery despite variable demand

examples.problem: Internet packet routing under heavy load
examples.solution: TCP congestion control, load balancing, adaptive routing protocols
examples.outcome: Stable throughput with minimal packet loss

examples.problem: Ant colony food distribution across foraging trails
examples.outcome: Near-optimal path discovery without central control

examples.problem: Emergency room patient flow during surges
examples.solution: Triage protocols, overflow routing, dynamic staffing
examples.outcome: Reduced wait times during peak demand

patterns.name: Rapid Spread Through Connected Population
patterns.abstractDescription: An entity (information, disease, behavior, fire) propagates through a connected network. Spread rate depends on connectivity, susceptibility, and containment barriers.

examples.solution: Vaccination, quarantine, contact tracing, social distancing

examples.problem: Fake news propagation on social media
examples.solution: Fact-checking nodes, algorithmic dampening, media literacy

examples.problem: Malware and worm propagation through networks
examples.solution: Network segmentation, patch management, intrusion detection
examples.outcome: Contained spread to isolated network segments

examples.problem: Financial panic and bank run contagion
examples.solution: Circuit breakers, deposit insurance, central bank intervention

commonSolutions: Create structural barriers/firebreaks in the network

patterns.name: Uncertain Arrivals with Priority Queuing Under Limited Capacity
patterns.abstractDescription: Agents arrive unpredictably at a processing system with finite capacity. A priority mechanism determines service order. Delays cascade when arrival rate exceeds processing capacity.

examples.problem: Emergency room overcrowding and long wait times
examples.solution: Triage protocols, fast-track lanes, predictive staffing

examples.problem: Airport security queue congestion during peak travel
examples.solution: PreCheck lanes, dynamic staffing, automated screening

examples.problem: Network Quality of Service (QoS) packet prioritization
examples.solution: Weighted fair queuing, ECN congestion signaling
examples.outcome: Sub-10ms latency for voice/video packets under congestion

commonSolutions: Dynamic resource allocation based on queue depth

patterns.name: Decentralized Task Allocation Under Local Information
patterns.abstractDescription: A system of autonomous agents allocates tasks among themselves using only local information and simple communication rules, without a central coordinator.

examples.problem: Bee hive task allocation (foraging, nursing, building)
examples.solution: Age-based role switching, waggle dance communication, threshold response
examples.outcome: Efficient division of labor without central control

examples.problem: Warehouse worker task assignment across dynamic orders
examples.solution: Zone-based picking, local queue management, peer signaling
examples.outcome: Reduced walking distance and improved throughput

examples.problem: Swarm robotics search and rescue in disaster zones
examples.outcome: Rapid coverage without single point of failure

commonSolutions: Simple local rules producing global coordination
commonFailures: Deadlock when all agents wait for others

patterns.name: Delayed Feedback Oscillations & System Instability
patterns.abstractDescription: A control system attempts to maintain equilibrium, but delays between measurement, action, and system response cause overshooting and perpetual oscillations.

examples.problem: The Bullwhip Effect in multi-tier supply chains
examples.solution: Point-of-sale data sharing, reduced order batch sizes, vendor-managed inventory

examples.problem: PID controller hunting in industrial thermostats
examples.solution: Derivative gain adjustment, predictive feedforward estimation

examples.problem: Intention tremors in Parkinsonian motor control
examples.solution: Deep brain stimulation to override phase-lagged proprioceptive feedback

commonFailures: Amplifying actuator power to force faster correction
Measuring state at insufficient sampling frequencies
